about: What Shree-Lipi's own composers write for Unicode Devanagari in the Shree-Lipi 7 Devanagari fonts (SHREE-DEV7-*; the 4/5/6 SHREE-DEV-* fonts draw all of these codes the same way). Each row: the Unicode string, the preferred bytes (hex, one byte per glyph code: what the 7 composer types for it), and, when there are any, the other spellings the composer also accepts. Captured from S8DevU64.dll and S8Dev764.dll (Shree-Lipi nxt) by typing the same keys into both; tools/ShreeDevTruth builds and checks the shree-dev7 and shree-dev456 tables against it. Rows that end in a bare virama hold the composer's answer while it waits for the next letter (a half form); at the end of a word the table writes the visible halant instead, and "exceptions" says, row by row, what it writes ("the table writes <hex>: why") - as it does for every row the table spells otherwise.
